content.jointProblem: Can the company's historical grid samples be combined with proximal soil sensing and geostatistical or management-zone models to predict small salinity pockets in Tisa floodplain fields well enough to guide densified sampling only where needed? The first experiment would test model transfer from chernozem/prescription settings to alluvial and saline soils against denser reference sampling.

rationale.text: The researcher has directly studied whether ECa covariates can improve soil spatial estimates at the company's current 4 ha sampling density.

sources.quote: Co-kriging with ECa reduced MAE by 18–31% relative to ordinary kriging at the 4 ha per sample density

rationale.text: His management-zone work shows an approach for concentrating sampling where spatial variance is higher rather than densifying uniformly.

sources.quote: zone-based sampling captured 23% more variance in organic matter at 30% fewer samples

rationale.text: He has characterised ECa spatial structure in heterogeneous Vojvodina fields, which is relevant to detecting small-scale soil variation.

sources.quote: Range parameters varied from 54 m to 312 m across fields.

rationale.text: He has quantified how prescription algorithms transfer across farm holdings and linked transfer error to sensing-based soil dissimilarity.

sources.quote: Transfer error in prescribed N rate correlated strongly with ECa dissimilarity (Pearson r = 0.71)

rationale.text: He has experience with rapid sensing in salt-affected soil profiles, which is relevant to the Tisa salinity problem.

sources.quote: The findings support the use of pXRF as a screening tool for profile characterisation in salt-affected soil surveys

rationale.text: He has worked on fusing multiple proximal and remote sensing streams into prescription workflows, matching the company's plan to add field sensing.

sources.quote: A key output was a Bayesian data-fusion framework that weights sensor contributions according to their field-specific predictive performance

rationale.text: The researcher has explicitly opened participation to joint projects with agri-tech companies.

sources.quote: joint projects with agri-tech companies developing variable-rate application hardware or farm management software

constraints.text: The plan depends on verified access to the company's historical archive of georeferenced samples and laboratory results; extraction, harmonisation and quality control of this archive must be part of the work.

sources.quote: Imamo GPS koordinate svih dosadašnjih uzoraka i laboratorijske rezultate za oko 18.000 tačaka iz poslednjih deset godina.

constraints.text: The solution must reduce or avoid additional dense grid sampling, because more field work, laboratory costs and longer delivery times conflict with the service price the company can charge.

sources.quote: Problem je što gušće uzorkovanje znači više terena, više laboratorijskih troškova i duži rok isporuke — a cena usluge nam već pritiska granicu prihvatljivosti za klijenta.

constraints.text: Any predictive layer must resolve salinity pockets much smaller than the current 4 ha grid, otherwise the company's standard map will continue to miss them.

sources.quote: slani džepovi postoje na površini od svega 0,3 do 0,8 hektara i da ih naša standardna mreža preskače.

constraints.text: The collaboration requires field access to commercial Tisa-area farms and a joint data-use agreement covering soil sampling and yield monitor data.

sources.quote: Prefers collaborations where field access to commercial farms is part of the arrangement
Most receptive to industry partners willing to share yield monitor and soil sampling data under a joint data-use agreement.

constraints.text: Company development capacity is limited to two developers and one GIS specialist at up to one-third time, with occasional field-team support, so the work plan must fit that capacity.

sources.quote: Imamo dva programera i jednog GIS specijalista koji mogu da odvoje do trećine radnog vremena za razvoj novih funkcija, uz povremenu podršku terenske ekipe za testiranje u polju.

risks: The researcher's spatial modelling evidence is largely from chernozem and nitrogen prescription contexts, while the company's problem is small salinity pockets in alluvial/floodplain soils near the Tisa; this transfer gap must be tested in the first experiment, not assumed.
The company previously found that satellite NDVI did not clearly reveal salinity in early spring, so vegetation-index-only prediction may fail for this target.
It is unknown whether the 18,000-point historical laboratory archive contains salinity-relevant measurements, consistent depths and sufficient positional accuracy for small-pocket prediction.
Researcher availability is unknown and could limit fieldwork and modelling capacity.
The company's price pressure and delivery-time constraints may conflict with the field validation needed to prove that adaptive sampling is reliable.
The company's limited development capacity could slow integration of any predictive layer into its portal.
questions: Does the researcher have availability and capacity for a joint project in the company's timeline, and what would the first 6–12 month work plan be?
Which salinity-relevant variables, depths, analytical methods and positional accuracy are present in the 18,000-point historical laboratory archive?
Can the company provide field access to Ravnica Agro or comparable Tisa-area fields, plus yield monitor and sampling data, under a joint data-use agreement?
What accuracy, minimum detectable pocket size, false-positive tolerance, sample budget and delivery time would make the adaptive sampling service operationally acceptable?
Which sensing route should be tested first: EM38/ECa, drone multispectral, pXRF, vis-NIR, or a fusion, and what equipment is already available?
Is the company also interested in an industrial PhD format, given that willingness for industrial PhD supervision is currently unknown?
